entities.summary:
Belgium, officially the Kingdom of Belgium, is a country in Northwestern Europe, bordered by the Netherlands, Germany, Luxembourg, and France. With 11 million people in 30,688 km², Belgium is one of Europe's most densely populated and highly urbanized countries. Despite its small size, Belgium has been one of the most historically significant territories in European history — a crossroads of cultures, languages, and conflicts.

Belgium's territory, historically known as the Spanish Netherlands and then the Austrian Netherlands, was the site of many of Europe's most decisive battles: Waterloo (1815), the Marne (nearby, 1914, 1918), Ypres (1914–1918), and the Bulge (1944). Its current borders were established by independence from the Netherlands in 1830 — an independence revolution notable as one of the first successful national self-determination movements in the 19th century. Belgium industrialized earlier than any continental European nation after Britain — the Liège-Charleroi industrial basin was Europe's first industrial region — making it briefly the world's second-largest industrial economy in the 1840s.

Belgium's linguistic divide between Dutch-speaking Flanders and French-speaking Wallonia has structured its politics for 150 years and produced the world's most complex federal system. Leopold II's Congo Free State (1885–1908) was one of the most brutal colonial enterprises in history. Today Brussels hosts the headquarters of the European Union and NATO, making Belgium the administrative capital of Western multilateral institutions.
